A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Overton pluralism study. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison, including material moved or renumbered between versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original human-study results with 1,209 participants, pilot experiments, automated judge evaluations, and clustering and robustness analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains the original empirical evaluations, reports a revised participant count of 1,208, and adds calculated reference-baseline results.

M1.justification: The voting-based clustering, representation threshold, coverage metrics, and Gemini 2.5 Pro FS+FR judging procedure are unchanged. Appendix I retrospectively describes earlier research directions; it does not establish a method change from v1.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 15 Model Slant and 45 PRISM questions, U.S. participant population, and pilot question coverage. No new evaluated domain or task is introduced.

E2.justification: Section 4.1 adds two constructed comparators: covering one viewpoint per question and covering the largest viewpoint under the weighted metric. The evaluated LLM roster and automated-judge comparison methods remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The reported main-study sample changes from 1,209 to 1,208 participants and from 29,016 to 28,992 ratings. The PDFs do not explain whether this reflects correction or exclusion. Question assignments, rating procedures, metrics, and clustering settings otherwise remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The prompting ablations, threshold sensitivity tests, cluster-size and difficulty analyses, clustering validation, and subgroup checks are retained. The political-slant analysis moves from v1 Appendix B to v2 Section 4.2 without new analytical findings.

E5.justification: Both versions retain three judge runs, five clustering seeds per configuration, bootstrap confidence intervals, cluster-robust regression errors, and 5,000-permutation subgroup tests. Revised confidence-interval and p-value entries do not change the statistical reporting procedures.

E6.justification: Tables 3, 4, 6, and 8 contain limited numerical revisions; for example, Llama 4 Maverick's adjusted weighted score changes from 0.490 to 0.484 overall and from 0.549 to 0.540 on PRISM. New reference scores are 0.169 and 0.524. Appendix A.1 also corrects result descriptions that contradicted v1's tables. These are reported revisions, not established same-setting performance improvements.

T1.justification: The coverage and OvertonScore definitions, weighted variant, clustering equations, and cohesion definitions are retained. The new reference baselines apply existing metrics without introducing new theoretical results or proofs.

C1.justification: The central contributions and claims remain the human-grounded coverage metric, representative study, low model coverage, and automated evaluation with rank correlation 0.88. The explicit release contribution and conclusion's domain-dependent qualification already appeared elsewhere in v1.

C2.justification: Section 4.1 newly suggests that heterogeneous representation ratings within larger clusters may explain failures against the largest-viewpoint baseline. Appendix I adds specific rationale concerning NLI failures on long or multi-claim text and the limitations of coarse stance grouping.

D1.justification: v2 adds explicit GitHub code and Hugging Face dataset links, whereas v1 only mentions their release. However, it removes the identification of OpenAI's text-embedding-3-large from the semantic-similarity baseline description. Other implementation details are largely retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Fulay et al. (2024) to the political-bias literature. Appendix I also acknowledges that the distinctive contribution lies in the specific human-grounded methodology rather than being the first pluralism evaluation. The main related-work comparisons remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 introduces the OVERTONBENCH name, moves the existing slant comparison into Section 4.2, adds an appendix overview and research-process narrative, and makes localized prose corrections. Most methodological and experimental exposition is retained.

P2.justification: Figure 2 changes from bars to horizontal points and intervals with baseline lines and significance markers. v1's slant-comparison Table 13 becomes v2's Figure 3 scatterplot, while the earlier standalone MAE Figure 3 is removed but its results remain. Most other figures and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: The new reference baselines improve interpretation of coverage scores, Appendix A.1 corrects misleading PRISM result descriptions, and explicit code/data links improve access information. These are useful, limited gains to an otherwise stable study. They are tempered by removal of the embedding-model identifier and residual inconsistencies, including Appendix A.3 still describing only one significant PRISM underperformer despite Table 6 showing two.
